A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StPR framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing reliable matching across revisions, relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original StPR results on UCF101, HMDB51 and Kinetics400, alongside component ablations, routing comparisons and distillation experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and additionally reports SSv2 evaluations, stationarity tests and routing heatmaps.

M1.justification: The frozen CLIP backbone, shared adapters, FSSD importance weighting, temporal decomposition, expert routing and training losses remain unchanged. Appendix A retains both algorithms. Equation notation corrections and shortened encoder descriptions do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual Something-Something V2 evaluation under two incremental protocols (Table 2), substantially extending benchmark coverage. UCF101, HMDB51 and Kinetics400 remain; v1's reference to four datasets did not include SSv2 experiments.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds L2P, S-iPrompts and ST-Prompt† to the existing UCF101/HMDB51 comparison. Its Kinetics400 table adds CSTA (Vivit) and CSTA (Times). These expand the evaluated comparator set beyond merely extending existing baselines to SSv2.

E3.justification: V1 defines final accuracy and backward forgetting; v2 additionally defines average accuracy, explicitly uses it in Table 1, and adds it alongside final accuracy in the ablation table. V2 also introduces SSv2 protocols with 84 base classes and 9 or 18 incremental tasks, plus eight-frame KPSS testing. The stated backbone, optimization budget and video sampling remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds empirical testing of the temporal-stationarity assumption (Figure 3) and task-selection heatmaps for three sampled label sets (Figure 5), while removing v1's computational-complexity analysis. Existing component, routing, distillation and hyperparameter analyses remain; the relocated hyperparameter sweep and task-wise ablation plots are not new experiments.

E5.justification: V2 introduces KPSS p-value distributions and thresholds of 0.05 and 0.02 for its stationarity analysis. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds or confidence intervals for benchmark accuracy, so this statistical addition is confined to the new diagnostic.

E6.justification: V2 adds SSv2 accuracies of 40.79 and 37.30, new comparator results, average-accuracy ablations and diagnostic findings, while removing cost results. Table 1 replaces final-accuracy reporting with average accuracy: UCF101 5×10s changes from 85.79 to 92.13, which is not a same-metric gain. The matching UCF101 10×5s full-model ablation changes from 88.52/6.39 accuracy/forgetting to 88.85/6.31, although v2 Tables 5–6 retain the old pair. StPR's Kinetics400 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects the classification-score expectation: v1 Equation 25 contains an extra mean-to-variance factor that is removed in v2 Equation 24, making this step consistent with main-text Equation 6. The central semantic-importance formula and temporal-decomposition reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list extend the state-of-the-art performance claim to SSv2. The central contributions—FSSD, TD-MoE and an exemplar-free framework with task-ID-free inference—retain their original meaning and scope.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes higher final accuracy from rehearsal methods' lower forgetting on Kinetics400 and interprets the new diagnostics as supporting stationarity and task routing. It removes v1's specific limitation concerning text–video alignment in medical or industrial domains. Most existing mechanism explanations remain.

D1.justification: V2 removes the supplementary encoder implementation expansions, tensor-shape and parameter/FLOP accounting, and the statement locating code in supplementary materials. Main-text hardware, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs, attention configuration and sampling details remain, as do both algorithms. The PDFs establish reduced documentation, not an actual change in code availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for CSTA, Something-Something, space-time prompting and S-Prompts, and positions ST-Prompt† and CSTA as leading competitors. The broader research positioning remains stable. Its classification of CSTA as exemplar-based conflicts with the exemplar-free description in reference [8]'s title.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and parts of the results discussion, compresses related-work and method explanations, consolidates appendix headings, and removes the Limitations and Potential Impact sections. The main section sequence and most of the narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the SSv2 table, stationarity histograms and routing heatmaps; expands the ablation table with average-accuracy columns; and removes the computational-cost table. The hyperparameter table moves from the main text to Appendix C.1, and v1 Figure 3 becomes appendix Figure 7. These substantially reorganize the experimental presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: SSv2 evaluation and the added prompt/CSTA comparisons provide a broader test of the claimed accuracy advantage. Separating average from final accuracy and correcting the appendix derivation also improve clarity. These gains are tempered by removal of encoder/cost documentation and the concrete domain-gap limitation, plus new inconsistencies in UCF101 results across Tables 4–6 and CSTA's exemplar classification. The overall improvement is useful but limited.
